label: Canonical URL
subject: page
reaches: the page as everyone else sees it
use: The thing is already live. Always prefer it.

label: ?use= lib pin
subject: page
reaches: anything lib/ or dist/ does, including what it does to the tab itself
misses: the page's own inline shell: its markup, and any x-data defined in the file
use: The change lives in lib/ or dist/ and the page file itself is unchanged.
trap: Pages serves the page FILE from the default branch, so a shell change shows the old shell wrapped around new lib, silently and with nothing reporting the mismatch.

label: Toss, address mode
subject: page;file;data;fileset
reaches: the branch's real page file, shell and all; with refs= on the renderer, each repository, file or folder the page's code reads at a ref of its own (?lib=<ref> is the web-tools entry), including one changed library file over an otherwise unchanged build; and a routed toss's viewer page
misses: anything the shell does to the TOP-LEVEL document (title, favicon, history, navigation), and anything the SHELL contributes to the view: the FAB and the Alpine bundle come from the default branch whatever ref the address names, so a branch change to lib/alpineComponents/fab.js needs the ?use= pin on a deployed page instead; and a tossed page's relative images, CSS url(), import() and iframes, which load from the deployed site
use: The change is in a page's own shell, or the page and what it reads belong at different refs: add refs= (or ?lib=<ref>) to the renderer's query, never ?use=. With nothing selected, a web-tools page runs its own ref and any other repo's page runs main.
trap: The change is in a page's own shell. The @<ref> pins the SUBJECT, which is what carries the branch's lib into the framed page; never add ?use= to the shell, which on an iPhone kills Safari's web process when the shell is also hosting a frame (measured by matrix on the device, 2026-09-08; the mechanism is not yet established). With a full SHA the address runs past the 150-character MCP body cap, which wraps it in backticks and defangs the link: hand it over in the chat caption rather than trimming it, and check a body with scripts/mcp-link-safe.py.

label: Toss, a composition of main and the branch
form: pages/toss-render.html?refs=owner/repo@<main sha>&refs=owner/repo@<branch sha>:<changed path>&…#gh=owner/repo@<main sha or branch sha>:<page>
subject: page;file
version: main at a pinned commit, with each file the branch changed read at the branch's commit
reaches: the tree a merge would produce, for the files the branch changed, when main changed none of them since the branch point and the branch removes or renames none; npm run showing checks both and offers it only then
misses: files a merge regenerates (dist/, the hook's whole generated files, the derived-csv catalogs), which are read at main and named; and, when the conditions fail, the merge itself: whole-file replacement would drop main's edits to a file both sides changed, so the script links the branch as it stands and says so
use: A web-tools branch that lags main, previewed as it would merge. npm run showing offers it once main's renderer and build read path entries; composing versions by hand with refs= is always available.
trap: Not a merge preview when a file changed on both sides, or when the branch deletes or renames a file; the script refuses it then rather than claiming it. Past 20 changed files it steps aside for the branch as it stands.

label: Toss, the framing app
subject: page
reaches: the app carrying the branch's copy of the framed page, and the app's own files
misses: the framed page addressed on its own, which is the route the session store recorded as wrong most often; pixels, since the frame fetches on the viewer's token and a headless shot comes back empty
use: The repo's .web-tools.json names the app under showing.app, and the change is under a declared view's prefix or the app's own folder. No ?use=: the renderer is web-tools main and the ref belongs to the framed repo. A ?lib=<ref> on the renderer picks the Web Tools code, and the app hands it on to every view that names none of its own.
trap: The address runs past the 150-character MCP body cap with a full SHA; in a PR body drop it to the chat caption rather than trimming it by hand.

label: Nested toss
subject: page
reaches: the renderer's own internals: routing, frame mounting, rendering, address parsing
misses: the top-level document, same as above; a nested shell is never the tab
use: The change IS toss-render. Address the branch's renderer, hand it the page as a trailing fragment.

label: Toss, carried payload
subject: page
reaches: any reader, no token, nothing hosted
misses: same-repo relative dependencies; only absolute-URL CDN deps resolve
use: The reader has no token, or you want the bytes pinned into the link itself.

label: Claude artifact
subject: page
reaches: a reader in the Claude app, where the GitHub token may be absent
misses: anything needing the network: artifact CSP blocks every external request
use: The link will be opened in the Claude app AND the page can be baked self-contained.

label: No link reaches it
subject: page
misses: everything: ?use= keeps the old shell, and a toss is never the top-level document
use: Send an inspected headless screenshot and say plainly that no link can show it. The escape is not a better link but moving the code into lib, where ?use= reaches it.
